newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SORENSTAM SOARS TO 77 IN FIRST ROUND OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SORENSTAM SOARS TO 77 IN FIRST ROUND OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.

text.p: Two-time defending champion Annika Sorenstam was close to tears after a nightmarish first round at the U.S. Women's Open on Thursday.
"I felt prepared and ready to go. I don't know what happened," Sorenstam said after posting six-over-par 77 in intermittent light rain on the Pumpkin Ridge course.
It was her worst round of the year on the LPGA Tour, and it left the Swede needing a monumental comeback to have a chance of becoming the first woman to win the championship three years is a row.

"I haven't given up at all," she said. "This is just Thursday. We've got three more days. I know how to play this course. I'm not going to leave here until I beat it. I'm going to try and forget about this round."
Sorenstam had one birdie and three bogeys in her first six holes, before making a triple bogey at the par-4 ninth, where she nearly lost her ball after hitting an errant second shot into thick hay.
She found the ball barely 20 seconds before the allowable five minutes had expired, took two shots to hack it out of the hay, then three-putted from the fringe.
"I was a little confused. As far as I can remember, the last three or four years I haven't been five over par after nine holes," she said.

"It was like, where am I, what am I doing? How do I get away from this? Take me away from here. It was not fun. Luckily I made only one bogey on the back nine, so it wasn't as bad as it could have been."
